summary: Ghost credit line labeled 'annotator-tool-offset' appears on finalized invoice after batch job (no matching tool invocations)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a negative adjustment (credit) labeled 'annotator-tool-offset' on their finalized invoice for billing period ending 2026-02-28. The credit amount is -$123.45 and appears on line item ID L-7743. AnnotateAI asserts they did not trigger any annotator tool invocations for the affected timestamps and their job logs show no tool calls.

Impact:
- Customer-facing: unexpected credit/line on finalized invoice causing internal reconciliation noise and requests to finance (AnnotateAI).
- Financial reporting: unexplained retroactive adjustment on finalized invoice.

Environment:
- Customer: AnnotateAI Ltd (dedicated tenant on prod-us-east).
- Workload: nightly batch annotation (bulk-embed then annotator enrichment), normally uses reserved hours.

Steps to reproduce / data to check:
1) Inspect finalized invoice ID INV-2026-02-28-A for line item L-7743.
2) Query billing audit logs for postbacks and dedupe fingerprints for tenant annotateltd (tenant_id: T-9182) between 2026-02-27T22:00:00Z and 2026-02-28T04:00:00Z.
3) Cross-check metric streams: toolcall_meter (tool=annotator), embed_meter, and postback ack logs.
4) Check job run logs from customer's submitted run (run_id: run-20260228-114) provided by customer.
5) Verify whether a postback replay or service-side retry created a synthetic negative adjustment.

Expected behavior:
No credit line appears on finalized invoice unless there is an explicit refund/adjustment request or identifiable postback-level dedupe that cancels previously-billed usage.

Actual behavior:
A single negative line labeled 'annotator-tool-offset' for -$123.45 appears. Customer job logs show zero annotator tool invocations during that window. Billing postbacks show a short-lived entry with an anonymous fingerprint that was later reversed.

Attachments / logs referenced:
- Customer job log (run-20260228-114) (uploaded by customer in initial message)
- Internal billing trace: trace_id=trace-bill-8842 (linked in Confluence page above)
- Invoice PDF INV-2026-02-28-A (attached by customer)
comments: 2026-03-10 10:12 - Maya Chen (Support): Logged ticket after customer called into billing team. Customer attached invoice and job logs. Acknowledged receipt and asked for time window and tenant id.

2026-03-10 10:35 - AnnotateAI (Customer): Confirm tenant_id T-9182. Provided run_id run-20260228-114. We saw no tool invocations in our sidecar logs. Please advise — finance is asking for an explanation.
2026-03-10 12:01 - Liam O'Connor (Support): Assigned. Requesting billing postback logs and trace. Adding billing and metering owners. Will investigate dedupe logic and postback replays.

2026-03-11 09:20 - Priya Rao (Billing Engineer): Found a reversed postback entry for tenant T-9182 with fingerprint fp-3f7c. There is an associated 'suppressed_retry' tag in the intermediate queue which triggered a compensation credit flow. Investigating why fingerprint did not associate with an original charge.

2026-03-11 14:45 - SRE (Evan Park): Observed a short outage in postback-processor between 2026-02-28T23:58Z and 2026-02-29T00:02Z. Some ack messages were processed out of order; dedupe window calculation may have been impacted. Continuing analysis.

2026-03-12 16:18 - Liam O'Connor (Support): Applied provisional customer credit for $123.45 to offset line L-7743 while we finish the audit. Noted this will be reconciled in next billing cycle if root cause confirms internal misclassification. Customer notified via email and accepted provisional credit.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: postback replay/dedupe-mismatch created a synthetic reversal entry that manifested as a credit on the finalized invoice.

Billing trace (trace-bill-8842) shows three postback events for the same batch window: an initial usage postback (status=accepted), a delayed replay with missing origin header (status=replayed), and a compensation entry generated by the 'suppressed_retry' handler.

Dedupe key generation changed in billing-service deploy 2026-02-27 (PR #1228) — new fingerprinting dropped the original 'origin' field in certain queued cases. Edge case affects multi-step workloads that invoke toolcalls after embeds in the same batch window.

Outage in postback-processor caused reordering; the 'replayed' entry lacked necessary meta to match original fingerprint, so compensation flow created a negative line rather than linking to original charge.

Customer-side logs (run-20260228-114) show embeds completed but annotator tool ran on an external worker that did not emit toolcall headers due to sidecar restart — supports hypothesis that server-side lost 'origin' header and generated orphaned compensation.

Reproducibility: low — requires sequence of (1) sidecar restart dropping origin header, (2) postback-processor outage causing reorder, (3) billing-service fingerprint change. Combined rare but occurred for this tenant.
resolution_notes: Provisional action: applied immediate credit of $123.45 to customer account (credit ID CRED-2026-03-12-58). Notified customer and Finance.

Code/ops action: reverted fingerprinting change for queued postbacks in billing-service (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/1236) to restore origin-based dedupe for hybrid batch flows. Backfill job scheduled to re-associate orphaned reversed entries across affected window (job id: backfill-bill-2026-03-13-02).
Monitoring: added an alert to detect 'orphaned_compensation' events and now count rapid >1 compensation events per tenant per 1h window. Alert runbook created on Confluence page referenced above.

Follow-up: billing engineering will run audit across Feb 27-29 for any additional tenants impacted. Support will update customer once audit completes and will close ticket after postback backfill finishes and finance confirms no further adjustments required.
resolution: Provisionally credited $123.45; code change merged to billing-service to fix fingerprinting on queued postbacks; follow-up audit scheduled
